parts.text: Variant: one change of the candidate model (the penalty chosen by nested cross-validation, a stronger or weaker regularisation, the model without one group of variables, or another model family), compared under the same evaluation; at most three, each with its question. Each configuration compared on the same rows is a trial; the more trials, the more the best of them may owe to chance. Recommended: The diagnostics of the linear model flag the shape of horsepower and weight: the Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM), a readable non-linear model, is drafted beside the penalty chosen by nested cross-validation to test it. Each variant spends one trial of the budget of three and adds a little selection optimism; the EBM, chosen after the diagnostics, is recorded as data-contingent. Boosting here is tree boosting, the same family as XGBoost and LightGBM. A random forest is not offered: a random forest usually does less well than a tuned boosting on tabular data, and a variant of the same kind would spend a trial for little new information. The diagnostics of the linear model show a pattern it cannot follow; a non-linear family may be compared as one variant (a trial, chosen after seeing the diagnostics).
